context: Dot density map of U.S. population by state using rejection-sampled stipple dots (1 dot = 10,000 people) on a geoAlbersUsa equal-area projection with interactive hover highlighting
first_impression: Encoding is fundamentally honest — equal-area projection enables valid visual density inference, dot count is directly proportional to population, and no deceptive size or color scaling is used.
what_works: Equal-area AlbersUsa projection ensures dots-per-screen-area reflects true population density; nDots computed as Math.round(pop/dotScale) is strictly proportional with no hardcoded domain ceiling.
what_doesnt: Shared seeded PRNG across states means dot positions shift for all later states if processing order changes (subset robustness failure); legend hardcodes NJ/WY density stats as string literals rather than deriving from data, and the computed maxDensity variable goes unused.
